title: The Borrowed Ledger
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, on the eve of a revolution that will topple the Merchant Assembly, Jonah Nakamura works her late father's type cases in a print shop that has become a quiet refuge for dissidents. When a sealed letter arrives naming her family as conspirators in a plot they never joined, Jonah realizes someone is using the shop's presses to forge evidence against the opposition — and that the victors intend to write history before the blood dries. Racing the advancing armies, she and a disgraced archivist, Elias Vane, print the true ledger of the Assembly's crimes and smuggle it out through the burning city. The revolution succeeds, but its new historians begin erasing inconvenient truths, and Jonah must choose between safety and publishing under her own name; she prints the borrowed ledger openly, loses the shop, and gains something rarer: a record no one can carry away.
about_author: Astrid Okafor is a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring colonial-era printing archives in West African port cities. She writes historical fiction about the people who keep records when power would prefer they didn't.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sorts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the Nakamura print shop, Jonah sets type for a merchant's wedding announcement while measuring everything in the house by what could be carried if soldiers came, as her mother taught her. A routine day establishes the family trade, the city's unease, and Jonah's habit of reading the world as movable pieces. Emotional beat: tender vigilance.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dusk
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Rumors of the Merchant Assembly's crackdown reach the docks; customers stop paying in coin and start paying in warnings. Jonah's brother Tomas urges the family to flee inland, but their mother refuses to abandon the shop where their father died. Emotional beat: the first fracture between staying and going.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A courier delivers a sealed letter bearing an official crest, naming the Nakamura family among signatories of a seditious plot. Jonah recognizes the typeface of the enclosed 'confession' — it was set on their own press, with their own worn ligatures. Emotional beat: cold recognition turning to fear.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Debt
chapters.summary: Elias Vane's POV. A dismissed government archivist comes to the shop seeking a hiding place for documents he refused to burn. He confirms the forgeries are part of a campaign to justify mass arrests once the revolution begins. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of shared guilt.

chapters.title: Ligatures Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah demonstrates to Elias how the forged confession matches their father's custom punctuation cuts, proving someone inside the conspiracy had access to the shop. Suspicion falls on their apprentice, Rell, whose brother serves the Assembly. Emotional beat: trust curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: What Mother Carried
chapters.summary: Mira Nakamura's POV. Flashback woven into present: Mira recalls fleeing another country decades ago with only a type case, and why she taught her children to measure life in portable things. She reveals the sealed letter echoes one she received long ago. Emotional beat: inherited displacement, quiet grief.

chapters.title: The Printer's Mark
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Following the watermark trail, Jonah and Elias trace the forged documents to a rival press run by Aldous Grebe, a printer who covets the Assembly's contracts. They find proof but also learn their names are already on an arrest list. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Rell's Two Brothers
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. The apprentice, caught between loyalty to the Nakamuras and his brother's demands, copies the arrest list and slips it under the shop door. His chapter reveals he did not forge anything but knows who did — and fears saying so will kill his brother. Emotional beat: divided heart.

chapters.title: Curfew of Ash
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The revolution ignites; barricades rise and the Assembly declares martial law. Soldiers search the district, and the family hides the true ledger pages inside hollowed type cases. The shop survives the night, barely. Emotional beat: terror held at bay by craft.

chapters.title: Reading by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias deciphers the stolen Assembly ledgers: debts, bribes, and orders for the massacre planned at Saltgate Wharf. He and Jonah realize the victors' historians will blame the massacre on the rebels unless the real orders surface first. Emotional beat: the weight of being the last witnesses.

chapters.title: Saltgate
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas witnesses the Saltgate massacre from a rooftop while trying to evacuate dockworkers, and sees Assembly officers directing it in rebel uniforms. Wounded, he carries back not just testimony but a dead officer's dispatch book. Emotional beat: horror and helpless fury.

chapters.title: Setting the Truth
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. By lamplight, the family and Elias set the true account of Saltgate in type — names, dates, orders — while cannon fire shakes the windows. Mira insists every victim's name be spelled correctly, even as ink runs low. Emotional beat: sacred, stubborn labor.

chapters.title: Grebe's Offer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Aldous Grebe arrives under truce flag: hand over the ledgers and the arrest lists burn; refuse and the mob outside will be told the Nakamuras are traitors. Jonah stalls him, buying hours, and discovers he answers to a historian already drafting the official version. Emotional beat: temptation and contempt.

chapters.title: The Mob at the Door
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Grebe's lie spreads; a crowd gathers to burn the 'traitor' shop. Mira walks out alone and speaks to them in three languages, telling the story of a woman who fled with a type case, until shame thins the crowd. Emotional beat: courage as storytelling.

chapters.title: Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. To move the printed truth through checkpoints, Jonah disguises the broadsheets as wedding announcements and funeral notices — the same work her father loved. Rell guides them through tunnels he used for smuggling letters to his brother. Emotional beat: ingenuity as resistance.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Tunnel Mouth
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. Rell's brother finds them at the tunnel exit and must choose between family duty and the evidence in Jonah's satchel. He lets them pass but takes the officer's dispatch book as insurance, splitting the proof in two. Emotional beat: love complicating justice.

chapters.title: The Historian's Draft
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias infiltrates the Assembly's archive as the regime collapses and finds the official history already typeset — Saltgate blamed on rebels, the Nakamuras listed as martyred traitors. He steals the plates meant to fix the lie forever. Emotional beat: righteous theft.

chapters.title: Fire Takes the Shop
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Retreating soldiers torch the print quarter. Jonah saves only the type cases and the ledger proofs, watching her childhood burn, and understands at last why her mother measured life in what can be carried. Emotional beat: loss transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: The Reading at the Wharf
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. At Saltgate Wharf, before the victorious rebel council, Jonah publicly reads the true ledger and hangs the printed sheets along the burned quay so the crowd can read the victims' names themselves. Grebe's forgery unravels when Rell's brother surrenders the dispatch book. Emotional beat: catharsis, public and earned.

chapters.title: Victors' Ink
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The new government offers Elias a post writing the official history — if certain pages stay out. He refuses, and the offer becomes a threat. Meanwhile the council debates whether the Nakamura broadsheets are 'destabilizing.' Emotional beat: the revolution devouring its witnesses.

chapters.title: Printed Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Offered amnesty for silence, Jonah instead reprints the full ledger with 'Set by Jonah Nakamura' beneath the title, distributing copies through the old tunnel network. The council, fearing the crowd more than her, lets it stand. Emotional beat: defiant belonging — claiming name, city, and truth at once.

chapters.title: What Remains Legible
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, years later. In a rebuilt shop on the same street, Jonah teaches apprentices — including Rell's daughter — to set type, while the original ledger hangs framed beside the door, its edges still smoke-stained. Mira tends the garden where the forge once stood. Emotional beat: peace as an act of memory kept legible.
